criteria:

---
' and over '---
---
# Title
', with a property set (_icon plus _color, and _favorite), returns exactly one frontmatter block, so the output has two '---' lines and the body is kept. It fails today (four '---' lines). The repro .scratch/file-io-audit/repro/o10-frontmatter-fidelity/empty-frontmatter-block.test.ts is moved under src/tests as this red test.

extractRawFrontmatter and extractBody recognise '---
---
' and the CRLF form '---
---
' as an empty block: raw is an empty string (not null) and extractBody returns only the text after the block. Cases for non-empty blocks, no frontmatter and an unclosed fence keep their current results.

Folder flow, in src/tests/lib/features/file-icons/file-icons.service.test.ts: after setIconForPath writes the '---\n---\n' placeholder for a folder without a folder note, a following setIconColors on the same path produces content with a single block holding _icon and _color, not a stacked second block.
ensureFrontmatterLink on an empty block keeps its current output (existing ensureFrontmatterLink cases in properties.logic.test.ts stay green, unchanged).
Gate, frontend only: pnpm check + pnpm vitest run.

Failing test first, in src-tauri/tests/history_test.rs (same setup and TEST_LOCK pattern as the save_snapshot cases): save two snapshots for 'notes/old.md' with save_snapshot, call the new rename_history('notes/old.md', 'notes/new.md'), then get_file_history('notes/new.md') returns both snapshots and get_file_history('notes/old.md') is empty. It fails today (the command does not exist, so the file does not compile against it).

Folder rename is prefix-aware: rows for 'a/x.md' and 'a/sub/y.md' move to 'b/x.md' and 'b/sub/y.md' on rename_history('a', 'b'), while rows for 'ab/z.md' (a sibling sharing the prefix text) are untouched.

Snapshot contents survive the move: get_snapshot_content for an id from before the rename still returns the saved bytes, and a second snapshot saved at the new path de-duplicates against the moved rows as it would have at the old path.

The command is registered with the Tauri handler and the frontend contract (src/lib/contracts/commands.ts), and src/tests/lib/contracts/ipc.test.ts and src-tauri/tests/ipc_contracts_test.rs stay green.

Wiring test, in src/tests/lib/core/filesystem/fs.service.test.ts: applyPathChange (through renameItem and moveItem) invokes rename_history with the vault-relative from and to keys, once for a folder change, awaited together with rename_in_search_index and before the per-path forgetNote sweep. The call is skipped when either path is outside the vault. A rename_history failure is logged and does not abort the rename, the way a rename_note failure does.

Auto-move reaches the same leg: a move performed by auto-move re-keys the history rows (it uses the same applyPathChange path; one test or an asserted call path in the existing auto-move or fs.service tests).

A Trash restore to a suffixed path (trash.service.ts restoreItem) leaves the restored note's History panel reachable at the new path, tested in src/tests/lib/core/trash/trash.service.test.ts. If restoreItem does not go through applyPathChange, it calls rename_history itself.
After a rename the old path has no rows, so a new note created at the old path starts with an empty history (asserted in the Rust test above).
Gate, both: cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml + pnpm check + pnpm vitest run.

A toolbar change through rewriteViewFile (src/tests/lib/features/type-definitions/rewrite-view-file.service.test.ts) writes a file that still contains the .view's comments.

Failing test first, in src/tests/lib/core/editor/editor.service.test.ts (saveFileByPath describe, real editorStore): a dirty tab with savedContent 'base' and content 'base plus mine', while readTextFile for the path resolves 'base plus external'. After saveFileByPath(path), the external text is kept (a File History snapshot or a conflict copy holding 'base plus external' was created before the write) and writeTextFile then writes the tab content. It fails today (the external bytes are overwritten with no read and no copy).
When the disk content equals the tab's savedContent, saveFileByPath saves as before: no conflict copy, no snapshot of external bytes, no toast.
When a conflict is detected the user sees a toast that names the note and says the external version was kept.

The calendar path (frontmatter-write.service.ts tab branch, which saves through saveFileByPath) gets the same protection, tested in src/tests/lib/core/frontmatter/frontmatter-write.service.test.ts: a calendar write to an open tab whose file changed on disk keeps the external version before writing.
The disk baseline is refreshed after each successful write and after each reload, so a normal second autosave of the same tab does not report a conflict.

The existing test 'skips dirty tabs, editor always wins' (editor.service.test.ts, reloadExternallyChangedTabs describe) is changed only with the owner's approval, and the change is recorded in the commit message.
Gate, frontend only: pnpm check + pnpm vitest run.

Owner decision recorded in the Issue Notes: what a dirty tab does when its file changed on disk since it was loaded, one of (a) keep the external version as a File History snapshot or conflict copy, then save and toast, (b) reload from disk and drop the in-app typing, or (c) keep 'editor always wins'. The criteria above assume (a); (b) or (c) replaces criteria 1 to 4.

Failing test first, in src/tests/lib/core/editor/editor.service.test.ts (reloadExternallyChangedTabs describe, real editorStore): a clean tab for '/vault/a.md', readTextFile rejecting with a not-found error, reloadExternallyChangedTabs(['/vault/a.md']) leaves no tab for that path in editorStore.tabs. It fails today (the tab is kept and the next keystroke or calendar write recreates the file). The repro .scratch/file-io-audit/repro/o07-external-change/external-delete.test.ts is moved under src/tests as the matching red cases.

A dirty tab hit by the same not-found read stays open with its typed content, is marked orphaned, and autosave is suspended for it: after onContentChange and the autosave timer firing, writeTextFile is not called for that path and the path does not appear on disk. The user sees a prompt or toast saying the file was deleted or moved outside the app.

saveFileByPath (writeTab) writes with { create: false } for tabs opened from existing files, so a save after an external delete or rename rejects and does not recreate the old path. Existing saveFileByPath cases that assert the writeTextFile arguments are updated for the options argument. The three repro scenarios (external delete plus keystroke, external rename plus keystroke, calendar write after an external delete) end with the old path absent from disk.
The calendar tab branch in src/tests/lib/core/frontmatter/frontmatter-write.service.test.ts: a write to an open tab whose file was deleted outside the app does not recreate it.
A read that rejects for another reason than not-found (for example a permission error) keeps today's behavior: the tab is kept and the failure is logged at debug level.
Gate, frontend only: pnpm check + pnpm vitest run.

Failing test first, in src/tests/lib/features/file-history/file-history.service.test.ts (restoreSnapshot describe, real editorStore and fileHistoryStore): the dialog is open for '/vault/a.md' with a snapshot selected, tabs a.md and b.md are open and b.md is the active tab, then restoreSnapshot runs. a.md receives the snapshot content (tab content by path, or a direct write) and b.md keeps its content and gets no write. It fails today (the snapshot is written into the active tab b.md). The repro .scratch/file-io-audit/repro/o05-settings-history/file-history-restore-target.test.ts is moved under src/tests as this red test.

When the dialog's tab was closed while the dialog was open (Cmd+W) but the file still exists, Restore writes the snapshot to that file directly and no other note changes. When neither the tab nor the file exists, restoreSnapshot aborts, writes nothing, and shows an error toast.
When the dialog's file is the active markdown tab, Restore still dispatches through the editor view as a normal history transaction (existing restoreSnapshot cases stay green).

Board views: with no editorView (a .kanban, .canvas or .collection tab in its board view, where EditorView mounts KanbanView, CanvasView or CollectionView), restoreSnapshot updates the tab content by path and saves, so the tab content equals the snapshot and the file on disk is written. It never closes the dialog as a success when nothing was applied: it throws or toasts in that case.

openFileHistory clears selectedSnapshot and diffLines: open for A with a snapshot selected, then openFileHistory for B leaves fileHistoryStore.selectedSnapshot null and diffLines empty (openFileHistory describe).
The Restore confirm text names the file being restored, asserted on the rendered text in src/tests/lib/features/file-history/FileHistoryDialog.test.ts.
Gate, frontend only: pnpm check + pnpm vitest run.
